page: Amazon Web Services r8in.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors operating at up to 3.9 GHz. The instance provisions 32 virtual CPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading configured at two threads per core. System memory totals 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of memory per virtual CPU.

Network throughput is configured with a 50 Gbps baseline, facilitating high-rate inter-node data transfers in distributed systems. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data volumes and root filesystems depend on Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) or separate network storage services. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the instance, and hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent.

The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio allows resource-heavy software stacks to maintain substantial active working sets without overpaying for unused compute cores. Primary workloads suited for this configuration include distributed in-memory databases, memory caching layers, large enterprise database engines, and stream processing applications demanding significant memory capacity combined with high networking throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services r8in.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors running at 3.9 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores alongside 256.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Designed for high network demands, it delivers a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions such as Amazon EBS for persistent data storage. No discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs are included. Because of its memory-dense configuration and elevated network throughput, the r8in.8xlarge is well aligned for workloads requiring large in-memory working sets, such as distributed in-memory caches, relational database systems, memory-bound enterprise applications, and large-scale data processing pipelines.
